newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS BEAT SHARKS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS BEAT SHARKS AGAIN.

text.p: Sandy Moger had two goals and an assist and Bill Ranford turned aside 31 shots as the Boston Bruins remained unbeaten all-time against San Jose with a 4-2 defeat of the Sharks Monday.
Moger recorded his first career three-point game and his first multi-goal contest since Januray 28th, against the Montreal Canadiens.
"If we keep doing the job, I'm sure we'll (the third line) get the ice time we need," Moger said. "The last three or four games we've got three or four lines that are supplying the goal scoring."
Ranford stopped 26 shots in the first two periods.
At Florida, Chris Simon scored twice and Todd Krygier had a goal and an assist as the Washington Capitals posted their season-high third straight win with a 4-2 victory over the Florida Panthers.
Sergei Gonchar also scored and Peter Bondra and Andrei Nikolishin added two assists apiece for Washington, which has won four of its last five games.
Olaf Kolzig made 27 saves for his second straight win.
In Phoenix, Darren McCarty scored with 1:43 left in regulation to lift the Detroit Red Wings into a 2-2 tie with the Phoenix Coyotes.

The Coyotes and goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin had been nursing a 2-1 lead since midway through the first period when Jeremy Roenick and Chad Kilger scored goals 40 seconds apart before McCarty scored his sixth goal of the season to tie it.
Khabibulin made a pad save on Brendan Shanahan's stuff attempt but McCarty, from his back skate, was able to poke it past the goaltender.
Khabibulin finished with 34 saves, including four in overtime.

In Calgary, Theo Fleury scored his second power-play goal of the game 7:07 into the third period to snap a tie and set up Jonas Hoglund's insurance tally later in the period to lead the Calgary Flames to a 5-3 victory over the slumping New York Rangers.

Fleury's second power-play goal gave Calgary a 3-2 lead. Less than three minutes later, Fleury and Hoglund broke into the New York zone on a 2-on-1, and Hoglund flipped the puck in for his fifth goal.
Mark Messier and Graves also scored for New York, which fell to 1-5-1 in its last seven contests.
